nodes.label: Simatrix Platform
nodes.rationale: A platform of interactive simulations helping B.Tech students build intuition for engineering concepts across disciplines; each sim ships as a sandboxed iframe payload teaching as a Guided Stepper. Success = a struggling first-year understands the first step in 30 seconds and can verify a textbook problem.

nodes.label: Guided Stepper
nodes.rationale: A progressive-disclosure wizard that sequences one concept at a time, moving the learner through Orient then Intuition then Problem-solving; replaces the overwhelming all-controls-at-once dashboard.

nodes.label: Brand Personality (Patient, Encouraging, Clear)
nodes.rationale: A warm one-on-one tutor sitting beside the student; encouragement delivered only through tone and a quiet sense of progress, never through game mechanics (no points/streaks/badges/confetti/mascots). Reference lane: GeoGebra, Desmos, Wokwi, Falstad, Tinkercad.

nodes.label: Anti-References (Product Boundaries)
nodes.rationale: Five locked-out boundaries: Gamified EdTech, Glossy/architectural-viz aesthetic, Marketing-site polish, Hard industry-tool mimicry, and the Overwhelming dashboard; they set the boundary for visual, interaction, and copy decisions on every screen.

nodes.label: Seven Core Design Principles
nodes.rationale: Seven strategic principles that override taste in conflicts and apply uniformly across all disciplines: struggling-learner-first, one-idea-per-step, one-language-many-disciplines, show-real-values, educational-scaffolding-industry-vocabulary, inclusive-by-default, and quiet-chrome-loud-subject.

nodes.label: Design for the Struggling Learner First
nodes.rationale: The tie-breaker meta-principle: when a decision helps the confident student but risks losing the anxious first-year, the weaker learner wins. Deliberately NOT a RULES.md checklist item because it cannot be mechanically verified.

nodes.label: Quiet Chrome, Loud Subject
nodes.rationale: Every UI pixel that is not the simulation viewport stays quiet enough that the math/geometry is what the eye lands on; restrained color (~10% blue accent), minimal decoration, no surface that competes with sim content.

nodes.label: Module 1 — Foundations of Projection
nodes.rationale: Seven live 3D guided-stepper lessons on one shared engine: five intro lessons (reference planes, types of lines, dimensioning, four quadrants, first-angle projection) plus two simulations (Projection of Points, Projection of Straight Lines).

nodes.label: Module 2 — Orthographic Projection of Solids
nodes.rationale: The master codebase: six gated steps flattening a hard-edged solid (cube, prism, pyramid, cylinder, cone) to a 2D orthographic drawing, with a parameter dock, rotation priority hierarchy, and vertex labeling; every change funnels through one rebuild() pipeline.

nodes.label: Compare View
nodes.rationale: The main pane is always the live 3D scene; the 2D textbook drawing (or a live-rebuilt 3D view while folded) appears on demand in a floating Compare card, with a docked side-by-side split for Points/Lines.

nodes.label: Cinematic Reversible Fold/Unfold
nodes.rationale: The HP plane hinges flat onto the VP about the xy fold line and back again, either holding the learner's own 3D viewing angle (Points/Lines) or sweeping square-on (First-angle).

nodes.label: Lines Workbench
nodes.rationale: The expanded Compare split collapses the wizard for a true 50/50 and docks the live driver controls (True Length, distance HP/VP, theta, phi) under both panes (ADR-021) — the one deliberate exception to progressive disclosure, for the solve-and-verify phase.

nodes.label: Problem Library
nodes.rationale: Tiered textbook problems with hints revealed one at a time and a ±0.5-tolerant self-check that never auto-fills; the student dials the setup and the check lights green, making the sim a verification tool not a toy.

nodes.label: Inline Term Glossary
nodes.rationale: Dotted-underline terms open a tooltip on hover/focus/click fed by per-lesson TERMS data, providing an inline definition the first time a textbook term appears without replacing the term itself.

nodes.label: Dual Perspective/Orthographic Camera
nodes.rationale: Top/Front/Side orthographic quick-view chips with a perspective-to-ortho morph, plus clip-aware auto-zoom and a connector/projector declutter toggle.

nodes.label: Parameter Dock
nodes.rationale: Module 2's uiManager controls: base length, height, distance HP/VP, angle HP/VP, manual Y rotation; every slider paired two-way with a clamped numeric input tolerating a decimal comma.

nodes.label: Accessibility Commitments (WCAG 2.2 AA)
nodes.rationale: WCAG 2.2 AA target: color never the only signal (two-cue rule), contrast, full keyboard access with visible focus, reduced-motion honored, screen-reader announcements, and legibility-first Atkinson Hyperlegible typography. Accessibility is a defining goal, not a compliance afterthought.

nodes.label: Primary Persona — Struggling First-Year
nodes.rationale: The person every decision is optimized for: a first-year who finds orthographic projection abstract and intimidating, with no CAD/MATLAB exposure, who quietly assumes they are 'bad at this'. Used across self-study, classroom, and assessment contexts.
